result:
The creation and acceptance paths exist, but the complete email journey has a gap: **the invitation service never sends an invitation email or exposes the raw token needed for a working link.** Here is the lifecycle the code actually implements, in execution order.

The members page, `Page()` in `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/members/page.tsx`, first calls `loadTenantContext()` from `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/_lib/tenant-context.ts`. That resolves the organization, calls `getActor()` in `src/lib/actor.ts`, asserts the tenant scope, and computes feature flags. Actor resolution requires a valid session and an active, unarchived membership in that organization. The page then checks `can(actor, "member:read", …)`, loads members through `member-service.listMembers()`, and obtains a seat `LimitCheck` through `billing-service.checkLimit()`. It renders the invite form only when `can(actor, "member:invite", …)` allows it.

`InviteMemberForm()` in `src/components/domain/member/invite-member-form.tsx` defaults the requested role to `"member"`, repeats the invitation permission check, and disables submission when the supplied seat check says there is no room. `RoleSelect()` and `assignableRoles()` in `src/components/domain/member/role-select.tsx` prevent selecting a role above the admin’s own. On submission, `handleSubmit()` validates with `inviteMemberSchema` from `src/schemas/member.ts`: the organization ID must be a ULID, the email must be valid and at most 254 characters, and the role must be `admin`, `member`, or `viewer`. `emailSchema` in `src/schemas/common.ts` lowercases the address; `invitableRoleSchema` in `src/schemas/role.ts` excludes `owner`. These client checks provide feedback; the server validates again.

`inviteMemberAction()` in `src/actions/members/invite-member.ts` runs through `withAction()` in `src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts`. The wrapper validates the input first, then resolves the admin’s actor through `requireActorFor(input.orgId)`. The action checks `can(actor, "member:invite", …)`. In `src/lib/permissions.ts`, authorization checks tenant equality first, then the platform-staff bypass, then `ROLE_MATRIX`, which requires at least `admin` for invitations. Next, the action consumes one token from the organization’s `"member:invite"` rate-limit bucket, loads `getOrganizationSummary()`, and rejects if cached `usage.seatsUsed + 1` exceeds `getPlanLimits(plan).seats`. The plan ceilings in `src/config/plan-limits.ts` are 3, 10, 50, and unlimited.

The action then calls `inviteMember()` in `src/server/services/invitation-service.ts`, which delegates to `inviteMembers()` with a one-item batch. That service independently checks `assertOrgScope()` and `assertCan()`, consumes the rate limit again, requires the organization to exist, and counts **active members plus pending invitations** using `member-repository.countActiveMembers()` and `invitation-repository.countPendingInvitations()`. `wouldExceedLimit()` rejects the whole batch before any token is generated. Consequently, this page’s single-invite path spends two rate-limit tokens. The service’s seat check includes pending invitations, whereas the earlier action and page checks use cached membership usage. Also, “pending” in the repository means neither accepted nor revoked: expired invitations still occupy seats in this calculation. There is no creation-time check for an existing member with that email or another invitation to the same address.

Once those checks pass, `inviteMembers()` calls `randomToken(32)` from `src/lib/hash.ts`, producing a URL-safe token from 32 random bytes. It passes only `hashToken(token)`—a SHA-256 hex digest—to `insertInvitation()` in `src/server/repositories/invitation-repository.ts`. The `invitations` table in `src/server/db/schema/members.ts` stores a generated ID, organization ID, normalized email, role, inviter’s user ID, unique token hash, expiry 14 days ahead, null acceptance/revocation timestamps, and creation/update timestamps. **No membership row exists yet.**

The returned `Invitation` type in `src/types/member.ts` has a misleading field named `token`: `toInvitation()` in `src/server/repositories/_mappers.ts` fills it with the **stored hash**, not the raw token. A working `/invite/<token>` link must carry the raw token, because acceptance hashes the supplied value again. The service discards that raw token and emits only `member.invited` with organization, admin actor ID, creation time, email, and role. `registerActivityListeners()` in `src/server/services/activity-service.ts` records that event as an invitation audit entry. The action then revalidates the organization cache tag; `withAction()` additionally revalidates `"members"` and `"invitations"` and returns a stamped `ActionResult<Invitation>`.

There is an email template, `InviteEmail()` in `src/emails/invite-email.tsx`, whose `InviteEmailProps` include inviter name, organization name, role, `acceptUrl`, and expiry. `renderTemplate()` in `src/emails/render.ts` can render it. However, the invitation path calls neither rendering nor sending, and no `member.invited` subscriber sends it. Even `sendEmail()` in `src/server/services/email-service.ts` only logs recipient, subject, and HTML size. Thus the colleague receiving a usable mail link is not implemented by this path.

Assuming a valid raw-token link is supplied, `Page()` in `src/app/(auth)/invite/[token]/page.tsx` validates its **syntax** using `invitationTokenSchema` from `src/schemas/invitation.ts`: 32–128 characters, limited to letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens. It does not look up the invitation or check expiry at landing time. `getSessionPrincipal()` in `src/lib/session.ts` resolves the session cookie and checks session expiry. A signed-out visitor goes to `/login?next=<encoded invite path>`; the login page and `LoginForm()` preserve that destination and return there after `loginAction()` succeeds. A signed-in visitor sees an accept button. The optional `?org=<slug>` supplies a later navigation destination; it does not determine which organization receives the membership, and this query parameter is omitted from the signed-out return URL.

`InviteAcceptForm()` in `src/app/(auth)/invite/[token]/invite-accept-form.tsx` submits the hidden token to `acceptInvitationAction()` in `src/actions/members/accept-invitation.ts`. That action validates `acceptInvitationTokenSchema`, requires a valid signed-in `SessionPrincipal`, and calls `acceptInvitation(principal.userId, input)`. It bypasses `withAction()` because the user need not yet have an actor in the target organization.

`acceptInvitation()` hashes the supplied token and calls `findInvitationByTokenHash()`. This lookup is deliberately unscoped by organization: the stored invitation supplies the tenant. In order, it rejects a missing row, a revoked invitation, an already accepted invitation, and an invitation whose expiry is at or before now. It does **not** compare the logged-in user’s email with the invited email or require email verification. Possession of the token plus a valid session is enough. It then calls `findMember()` for the stored organization and signed-in user. If an unarchived membership already exists, it returns that membership without consuming the invitation or emitting a join event.

For a new member, `insertMember()` in `src/server/repositories/member-repository.ts` writes an active membership with the stored organization, signed-in user ID, invited role, original inviter, current join/creation/update timestamps, and null last-seen time. The service then calls `markInvitationAccepted()` and emits `member.joined`. Its typed payload, defined in `TaskflowEventMap` in `src/types/event.ts`, contains organization ID, joining user as actor, occurrence time, membership ID, user ID, and role.

The rest of the system receives that event through subscribers wired by `register()` in `src/instrumentation.ts` and `registerEventHandlers()` in `src/server/services/event-registry.ts`. `registerUsageListeners()` in `src/server/services/usage-service.ts` calls `usage-repository.incrementUsage()` to add one seat. The notification service’s `registerFanOut()` calls `notify()` to create a `"member_joined"` notification for the organization owner, filtered by preferences and excluding self-notifications. **There is no `member.joined` subscription in the activity or webhook listener registrations**, despite that event appearing in their supported vocabularies. `emit()` in `src/lib/event-bus.ts` awaits subscribers concurrently and isolates their failures; a subscriber failure does not roll back membership creation.

Only **after the membership, acceptance timestamp, and join event** does `acceptInvitationAction()` run `assertSeatAvailable()`. It resolves the new actor through `member-service.resolveActor()`, reads the organization summary, and rejects if cached seat usage is above the plan limit. This is a post-write check with no rollback: an over-limit error can leave the membership created and invitation consumed. Acceptance also performs no explicit cache revalidation.

On a successful result, `InviteAcceptForm()` navigates to the supplied organization slug or `/orgs`. The chooser’s `Page()` in `src/app/(dashboard)/orgs/page.tsx` calls `listOrganizationsForUser()`; `organization-repository.listOrgsForUser()` discovers the new organization through the membership row and redirects automatically when there is exactly one. Subsequent workspace requests use `session-service.resolveActorForOrg()` to read the active membership, construct an `Actor` with its stored role, assert tenant scope, and update last-seen time. That actor now drives permissions and feature-flag context throughout the workspace. Acceptance itself does not switch the session’s active organization.
